source: Axis GRC & Compliance Pain Research, 2026-10-11. Screenshot-weakness thesis: John Flack (GRC Engineering Club); Ann Wallace (Edera). Performative-GRC/self-authored thesis: Nirosh Jayaratnam.

types.label: Screenshot of a settings screen
types.why: One setting, on one screen, at one moment, chosen by the auditee. Stale within hours, cherry-pickable, point-in-time not period, and it can't show prevention.

types.label: Manual assertion / email confirmation
types.why: An assertion, not evidence. An auditor cannot reperform it.

types.label: Configuration export from the system of record
types.why: Pulled from the system of record; reflects the actually-enforced state, not a staged view.

types.label: Automated log / audit trail
types.why: A time-series record over the whole period; hard to cherry-pick a single moment.

types.label: Programmatic API pull
types.why: Reproducible and covers all resources, not a sampled screen.

types.label: Ticket / PR with approval
types.why: Shows the control operated with authorization and a reviewer, across many instances.

types.label: Independent or tool-generated report
types.why: Independent or tool-generated; not authored by the auditee.

types.label: Signed / dated record
types.why: A dated, attributable record of a real event.

types.label: Self-authored document
types.why: Proves a document exists, not that the control operated. Templates you didn't write and can't defend are the classic 'performative GRC' trap.

unclassified.why: Could not match a known evidence type. Treat as weak until you can tie it to a system of record.
unclassified.upgrade_to: tie it to a system of record (export, log, ticket, or report)
